newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares power ahead but seen losing steam.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares power ahead but seen losing steam.

text.p: Danish share prices closed on a new record on Friday, powered by the rising Dow and keen foreign interest in the Copenhagen market.
But a dealer said that the onset of the summer holiday season this weekend was liable to dampen trade next week.

"Liquidity in the market is good, but I think nevertheless we shall have a hard time staying at these high levels over summer. So I think that the market will go sideways or down a little on Monday, depending what is going on elsewhere in the world," he said.
The KFX top-20 index closed up 0.90 point, or 0.52 percent, at 173.04 in overall bourse turnover of 1.378 billion crowns.
The KFX August future rose 2.25 point to 173.85 with five contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

BG Bank rose 16 crowns to 365.00 crowns on continued rumours that it could be a merger candidate with a range of different banks. A Kleinwort Benson analysis described the talk as groundless and advised its clients to sell the stock, which it said had been pushed to an unreasonable level.
FLS rose 15 crowns to 229.00 on rising interest in engineering and cement industry paper.
